questions.q: What two-gate sequence builds |Φ+⟩=(|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2 starting from |00⟩?
options: Apply Hadamard to qubit 1, giving (|00⟩+|10⟩)/√2, then apply CNOT with qubit 1 as control and qubit 2 as target, giving (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2
Apply CNOT first, then Hadamard to qubit 2
Apply Pauli-X to both qubits simultaneously
Apply Hadamard to both qubits, then measure
questions.explain: This is the standard, verified recipe: H on qubit 1 creates the superposition (|00⟩+|10⟩)/√2, and CNOT then correlates qubit 2 with qubit 1, flipping only the |10⟩ term to |11⟩, producing exactly |Φ+⟩.

questions.q: In the proof that |Φ+⟩ cannot be factored into a product of two single-qubit states, where does the contradiction arise?
options: Matching coefficients requires ad=0 and bc=0, but ac=bc=1/√2≠0 -- forcing either a=0 (contradicting ac≠0) or d=0 (contradicting bd≠0), either way a contradiction
The contradiction arises because |Φ+⟩ is not normalized
There is no contradiction; |Φ+⟩ actually does factor into a product state
The contradiction arises because a and b must both be negative
questions.explain: Attempting to match |Φ+⟩'s actual amplitudes (zero on |01⟩ and |10⟩, nonzero on |00⟩ and |11⟩) against a hypothetical product state's coefficients leads directly to an unsatisfiable system of equations.

questions.q: What does the CHSH violation (|S|=2√2≈2.828 > classical bound of 2) actually prove?
options: That no local-hidden-variable theory -- where each qubit carries fixed, pre-determined, non-communicating answers -- can reproduce the correlations quantum mechanics predicts and experiments confirm
That faster-than-light communication is possible between entangled particles
That quantum mechanics is incorrect and must be replaced
That classical probability theory is entirely inapplicable to any physical system
questions.explain: CHSH violation specifically rules out local-hidden-variable explanations for the correlation strength -- it says nothing about faster-than-light signaling (which teleportation's need for a classical channel already rules out separately) and doesn't invalidate classical probability in general.

questions.q: In teleporting |ψ⟩=0.6|0⟩+0.8|1⟩, what correction does Bob apply if Alice's outcome is Ψ−, and what does his qubit become?
options: Bob's qubit starts at (−0.8, 0.6); applying X gives (0.6, −0.8), then applying Z gives (0.6, 0.8) -- the original state recovered
Bob's qubit starts at (0.6, 0.8) already; no correction is needed
Bob applies only Z, recovering (0.6, 0.8) directly from (−0.8, 0.6)
This outcome cannot be corrected, so teleportation fails 25% of the time
questions.explain: The Ψ− outcome requires the two-step correction X then Z (verified): X swaps the amplitudes to (0.6,−0.8), then Z flips the sign of the second amplitude to recover exactly (0.6, 0.8).

questions.q: Why doesn't Bob successfully ending up with |ψ⟩ after teleportation violate the no-cloning theorem?
options: Alice's original qubit is destroyed by her Bell measurement in the process, so at no point do both Alice and Bob simultaneously hold a copy of |ψ⟩ -- the state is relocated, not duplicated
No-cloning only applies to single-qubit gates, not multi-qubit protocols like teleportation
Teleportation does violate no-cloning, which is why it only succeeds with probability 0.25
Alice keeps a copy of |ψ⟩ the entire time, which is why teleportation works
questions.explain: No-cloning specifically forbids two independent copies existing simultaneously. Since Alice's measurement destroys her copy at the same moment Bob's information is extracted, there's never a point with two copies -- fully consistent with, not an exception to, no-cloning.
